answer: Each challenge commits to a future drand quicknet round, then derives its task and verification seed from that round’s threshold-BLS pulse. Until the pulse is published, participants cannot know the exact instance to solve, so cached work cannot be prepared in advance. Commit-reveal can bind each claim to its response, while pulse-dependent checks prevent reuse across identities. An automated sybil swarm must therefore do fresh work per challenge; inlet, relic, and willow are task labels, not secrets or trust assumptions.
